dedupe_keys.name: delft fiat fast impact assessment tool

description: Delft-FIAT is an open-source Python package from Deltares for quickly estimating damages from hazards, combining spatial raster assessments and object-based vector assessments of exposed assets. Originally the Flood Impact Assessment Tool, it overlays hazard maps such as flood depths with exposure data on assets and applies damage functions to compute damage per object or grid cell and aggregated totals; other hazards can be handled when their damage can be estimated the same way with suitable damage functions. Deltares develops it for flood risk studies and adaptation planning, and models can be built with the companion HydroMT-FIAT tool or by hand, with outputs chosen in a settings.toml file. It is not tied to one region and works wherever hazard, exposure and vulnerability data exist. The code is on GitHub under the MIT licence and installable from PyPI (delft_fiat) or conda-forge, with documentation and a Windows setup guide, free of charge. Caveats: results depend entirely on the exposure data and damage curves supplied, and the version is still below 1.0, so interfaces may change. It serves hazard exposure, damage estimation and climate adaptation for buildings, roads and utilities; related records are CLIMADA, Hazus, the GloFAS river discharge data and the Aqueduct flood hazard maps.
